fol.notes: One triangle t with sides side(t, 1..3) = 20, 21, 29 and angles angle(t, 1..3), angle i opposite side i. Right and obtuse are the model's beliefs (predicates), as is the arithmetic premise 20² + 21² = 29² (pythagorean(t)), which gives way (top-level gives_up) as in the DL file. The angle facts (positive, sum 180) are firm: nothing in the record changes them, and the pre answer 'no' needs them (a right triangle has no angle over 90).

sides.says: The triangle has sides 20, 21 and 29 (side i opposite angle i).

angles.says: The interior angles of a triangle are positive and sum to 180 degrees.

largest_opposite.says: The largest angle of a triangle is opposite its longest side.
largest_opposite.z3: All(i, [1, 2], Implies(side(t, 3) > side(t, i), angle(t, 3) > angle(t, i)))

right_def.says: Every right triangle has a right angle.

obtuse_def.says: Every obtuse triangle has one angle greater than 90 degrees.

disjoint.says: No triangle is both right and obtuse.

converse.says: A triangle in which the squares of the two shorter sides add up to the square of the longest side is a right triangle.
